**Setting up the count.** A nonempty subset with smallest element $a$ and largest element $b$ (where $a \le b$) must contain $a$ and $b$. Its other elements can be any subset of the integers strictly between them, which gives $2^{b-a-1}$ subsets for $a<b$.

**Singletons.** A singleton $\{a\}$ has smallest and largest element both equal to $a$, so the condition becomes $2a = 13$, which has no integer solution. So no singletons contribute.

**Pairs $(a,b)$ with $a<b$ and $a+b=13$.** Since $a<b$, we need $a \le 6$:

| $a$ | $b$ | $b-a-1$ | $2^{b-a-1}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 12 | 10 | 1024 |
| 2 | 11 | 8 | 256 |
| 3 | 10 | 6 | 64 |
| 4 | 9 | 4 | 16 |
| 5 | 8 | 2 | 4 |
| 6 | 7 | 0 | 1 |

**Total.**
$$1024+256+64+16+4+1 = 1365$$

ANSWER: 1365
